summary: Typhoon canceled a flight on a round the world trip, 26 hour delay
story: I am traveling around the world on a fixed schedule of eighty days with my traveling companion, Mr. Passepartout. On July 8 our flight from Hong Kong to Tokyo, from where we were to continue to Yokohama, was canceled because of a typhoon. We departed 26 hours later. I am claiming the hotel, our meals and the rebooking fee, which come to $580. I am also claiming $2,000 for a wager with members of my club in Boston, which I forfeited because the delay made me late for a stage of the journey we had agreed on. I keep precise records and every receipt is attached.

documents.name: Meridian Air cancellation notice
documents.content: Meridian Air. Flight MA 882 Hong Kong HKG to Tokyo NRT, scheduled departure July 8, 2026 at 10:05, was canceled because of Typhoon Signal No. 8. Passengers Phil Fogg and Jean Passepartout were rebooked on MA 884, which departed July 9, 2026 at 12:10. Rebooking fee charged: $150.00.

documents.name: Hotel receipt
documents.content: Harbour Grand Kowloon, July 8 to July 9, 2026. One twin room, guests P. Fogg and J. Passepartout: $310.00.

documents.name: Meal receipts
documents.content: Harbour Grand Kowloon restaurant, July 8, 2026, lunch and dinner for two: $88.00. Airport cafe, July 9, 2026, breakfast for two: $32.00. Total: $120.00.

documents.name: Letter from the club
documents.content: The Beacon Hill Reform Club, Boston, August 20, 2026. We confirm that Mr. Fogg forfeited a stake of $2,000 under the terms of a wager recorded in the club's book on May 29, 2026, having reached Yokohama a day later than the agreed date.
